clue.text: Big, dangerous adder seen in this year's fine weather?

parts.note: big means long, as in a big queue
dangerous means hot, as in a hot situation or hot goods
an adder is one who adds figures, so a summer, one who sums

explanation.surface: A large venomous snake has turned up in this year's lovely weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adder' looks like the snake but is one who adds up, a SUMMER; the question mark warns that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell of hot weather through the warm season is what the phrase names, and the clue pictures it as this year's fine spell.

clue.text: Old-fashioned crew-cut leads a vein

parts.note: something old-fashioned is out, no longer in fashion
a crew-cut is a short haircut, a crop

explanation.surface: An outdated short haircut is somehow linked with a blood vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vein' looks like a blood vessel, but here it is a seam of ore; rock exposed at the surface is what guides miners to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock showing at the surface is where a seam of mineral comes up, so it leads prospectors to the lode below.

clue.text: We're not bisons or okapi: we're sung about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the word sung are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Animals protest that they are neither bison nor okapi, though songs are written about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it is the anagram signal on SUNG; the animals, wildebeest, speak in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest are African antelopes, neither bison nor okapi, and the clue lets them say so themselves.

clue.text: Lord in a cycling number?

indicators.note: cycling means the first letter of the run Lord in a goes round to the back

explanation.surface: A peer appears to be a number in some cycling event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like riding a bicycle, but it moves the L of LORDINA from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as first, second and third are numbers that give position in a sequence.

clue.text: Triumph Spitfire, ultimate cult car, epitomises Swinging Sixties first of all

indicators.note: first of all tells us to take the opening letter of every word in the run before it

parts.words: Spitfire, ultimate cult car, epitomises Swinging Sixties

explanation.surface: The Triumph Spitfire sports car is held up as the cult car that summed up the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Triumph' looks like the make of the Spitfire car, but it is the definition, a victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or achievement.

clue.text: A friend for tea? …

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a friend is coming round for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue to 7-down, whose clue continues the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal in British slang, and the South American herbal drink brewed from holly leaves.

clue.text: … just the strange one situated near California

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the word the are put into an odd order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Continuing 6-down, only the odd one living near California is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns THE into ETH; 'situated near' simply joins ETH, I and CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being just means being morally right and fair, which is what principled behaviour is.

clue.text: See the striker wait for going-home time

parts.note: to see is to watch
a striking clock chimes the hours, so a striker is a clock

explanation.surface: Look at the footballer who scores goals, waiting until the end of the working day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer or a worker on strike, but it is a clock that strikes the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock-watching is idly waiting for the working day to end so you can leave.

clue.text: Like very modern Snow White with decisions left to the dwarfs?

definitions.text: Snow White with decisions left to the dwarfs?

explanation.surface: Snow White leaves all the choices to her seven little housemates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' is read as the adjective 'tiny', so leaving matters to the minute is leaving them to the dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fully current, and also says choices are left with the tiny ones, the seven small companions of the fairy tale.

clue.text: A report about time creates shock

indicators.note: about means the word for report goes round the time letter

parts.note: a report is a sound, such as the bang of a gun

explanation.surface: A news report on timing causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a news item but is a loud noise, SOUND, which 'about' wraps round T.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to amaze or stun them.

clue.text: Overtake trap on horseback

parts.note: to trap an animal is to catch it
a jockey is said to be up when riding, so on horseback gives the word up

explanation.surface: Pass someone while riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The racing convention is that the rider is 'up', as in 'Dettori up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw level with someone ahead after lagging is to overtake them.

clue.text: Worry about scripture lessons?

parts.note: ca, for circa, means about
RE, religious education, is the British school subject covering scripture

explanation.surface: Someone frets over Bible classes.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, the British school subject once called scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Care in the sense of anxiety or concern is a worry.

clue.text: Put to rest having rendered inert

indicators.note: rendered here means made over, so the letters of inert are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: Something was laid to rest after being made motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' looks like 'made', but it is the anagram signal on INERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to lay it to rest.

clue.text: Some hi-tech-organs reverberate

indicators.note: some means only part of the letters of hi-tech-organs is wanted

explanation.surface: Several modern electronic organs make the hall ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the hyphen in hi-tECH-Organs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that reverberates repeats as it bounces back, which is what a repeated sound does.

clue.text: Computer information involves inversion of bit and Greek character

indicators.note: inversion of means the words for bit and Greek character are each turned backwards in place

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Computer data apparently involves flipping a bit and a Greek letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like a binary digit, but it means a small amount; 'inversion of' turns each of the two pieces round where it stands rather than swapping their order.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item of data, a fact or figure, is a piece of information.

clue.text: Time for European member to be put to the test

annotationWithheld.why: Time for European member to be put to the test: T (time), E (European), MP (member) give only TEMP; nothing in the clue supplies the final T
annotationWithheld.clue: Time for European member to be put to the test

clue.text: Rework a spoilt canvas

indicators.note: rework means the letters of a spoilt are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: An artist repaints a ruined canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' looks like a painting, but it is sailcloth: the answer is a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails are made of canvas, so the word can stand for a sail.

clue.text: The last riot showed sly cunning

indicators.note: a riot is chaos, so the letters of the last are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The final uprising displayed crafty guile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' looks like the subject, but it is the anagram signal on THE LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by secret and furtive means shows craft, sly cunning.

clue.text: Motivate badly then employ

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of then are put in a wrong order

parts.note: to employ something is to use it

explanation.surface: A manager inspires staff poorly and then hires them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is the anagram signal; 'Motivate' is the definition in the sense of inspiring enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone with eagerness is to inspire and motivate them.

clue.text: I'm apt to play in elevated part of orchestra

indicators.note: to play means the letters of I'm apt are allowed to move freely
in a down clue elevated means the word in is written upwards

explanation.surface: A musician says they are ready to perform in the raised section of the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' turns IMAPT into TIMPA; 'elevated' turns IN upwards into NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums form the percussion section's best-known part of an orchestra.

clue.text: Spike's getting to blow it? I'll protect the listener!

parts.note: a spike of wheat or corn is an ear
to blow it is to muff, to bungle a chance

explanation.surface: Spike is about to ruin it, and a protector of hearing speaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a name, but it is a grain head, EAR; the definition speaks as the object.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded cover worn over each side of the head keeps the hearing organs warm, protecting someone who listens.

clue.text: Shipping order's scientific value is mass deception

parts.note: S/O is the trade abbreviation for a shipping order
pH is the scientific value for acidity
taken as written
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A shipping order's figures turn out to be a large-scale fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: pH is the chemist's measure of acidity; 'mass deception' looks like one phrase but splits after 'mass'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever but false argument meant to mislead is a form of deception.

clue.text: Inferior team to go down

parts.note: sub, as a prefix, means below or inferior
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A weaker team is facing relegation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go down' suggests relegation of a sports team, but here it means sink.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside is to sink or settle lower, as floodwater or ground does.

clue.text: Temp is elected — displaying exceptional merit

parts.note: a candidate elected is in

indicators.note: exceptional means the letters of merit are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A temporary worker has been voted in because of outstanding merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' turns MERIT into TERIM; 'Temp' is used as the adjective, short for temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap arrangement lasting only until something permanent is found is temporary.

clue.text: Such a duck would provide 7 a poor meal

indicators.note: poor signals the letters of meal are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An injured duck would make a disappointing dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A lame duck is an injured bird and, figuratively, an official who has lost power; the stray 7 in the clue as held plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective completes the phrase for a crippled bird or an ineffectual person, a lame duck.

clue.text: Crow family?

parts.note: the Crow are a Native American people, so the family is a people group, not a bird family

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like the bird and 'family' like a zoological grouping, but the Crow are a Native American nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a social group of related families, and the Crow nation is one.

clue.text: Overpower the returning bats

indicators.note: returning means the word for bats is read from the back

parts.note: bats means crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: Defeat the bats as they fly back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but is the adjective 'crazy', NUTS, which 'returning' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or knock out, overpowering someone.

clue.text: Sounds like top dog

indicators.note: sounds like means the answer is said the same as the word for top

parts.note: a peak is a top, a summit

explanation.surface: It sounds like the best dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top dog' looks like a phrase for the leader, but 'top' gives PEAK, and the answer is said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pekingese is a small toy breed of dog.

clue.text: The Derby, perhaps, but not this

parts.note: T is a dialect shortening of the, as in Yorkshire t'
a derby is the American name for a bowler hat, an example of a hat

explanation.surface: The Derby horse race, maybe, though not this one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the Epsom horse race but is a bowler hat; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun pointing to something further off is the counterpart of this.

clue.text: From whence comes French wine — and Perrier for Moggy?

parts.note: moggy is British slang for a cat, chat in French
Perrier is a French mineral water, eau in French

explanation.surface: A question about the origin of French wine, and whether Perrier is fit for a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: MOGGY is everyday British slang for an ordinary cat; with 'French' in the clue, cat gives CHAT and water gives EAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux wines are named after the country estate where the grapes are grown, so the estate is the wine's source.

clue.text: lady's sex-appeal

annotationWithheld.why: lady's sex-appeal (7): the clue is cut short; IN + HER + IT is visible but no definition or the word giving IN survives, and no search found the full text

clue.text: Magazine concerning age again and again

parts.note: Time is a famous American news magazine
after can mean concerning, as in asking after someone
an age is a time, an era

explanation.surface: A magazine about old age, appearing repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' could be a store of ammunition, but here it is the news weekly Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something repeatedly is doing it over and over, again and again.
